title: Surrounded by Idiots
author: Thomas Erikson
blurb: Thomas Erikson, a Swedish communication consultant, starts from a simple frustration: why do some people seem impossible to work with? His answer is that people behave in different, predictable patterns. Drawing on the DISC behavioral model, he sorts these patterns into four colors. Reds are driven, fast and results-focused. Yellows are sociable, optimistic and creative. Greens are calm, loyal and harmony-seeking. Blues are careful, analytical and detail-oriented. Most people are a blend, usually with one or two colors standing out. Erikson explains what each type values, how it sees the others, and where each one struggles. The real payoff is practical: once you recognise someone's style, you can adjust how you speak, write and give feedback so your message actually lands. The book offers a simplified model, not a scientific diagnosis, but a useful lens for everyday communication.

lessons.b: When people seem impossible to deal with, the problem is often a clash of communication styles, not a lack of intelligence.

lessons.b: Reds are fast, competitive and results-focused, so talk to them briefly, directly and about outcomes.
Yellows are sociable, creative and energized by people, so engage them with enthusiasm and vision, then help them follow through.
Greens value harmony, security and relationships, so approach them with patience, warmth and plenty of notice before change.
Blues care about accuracy, quality and logic, so bring them facts, details and time to think.
Each color sees the others' strengths as weaknesses, which is why fast-and-bold types and slow-and-careful types so often frustrate each other.
